name: RESUN
full_name: Radio EVLA Search for UHE Neutrinos
summary: A historical lunar-neutrino search at the Very Large Array used fast coincidence measurements across radio antennas to look for ultra-high-energy neutrinos interacting in the lunar regolith.
detection_principle: A neutrino-induced lunar shower can emit a nanosecond Askaryan pulse. Simultaneous voltage triggers in four radio antennas, corrected for geometric delays, discriminate lunar pulses from instrumental noise and terrestrial interference.

sites.name: Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array, Socorro, New Mexico
sites.location: Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array, Socorro, New Mexico

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The cited sources document historical observing campaigns and published limits; they do not establish continuous current neutrino-search operation.

timeline.event: First results and extended project description published.

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: RESUN-A geometry
key_parameters.value: One sub-array of four VLA/EVLA antennas

results.summary: No lunar-origin pulses were detected during 45 hours. The first-results paper reported 90% confidence flux upper limits rather than a detected neutrino flux.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
